findings.reason: without a stated requirement that the probe answer keep its existing per-tool name list (and that the child tolerate a probe carrying no registered parameters), a node implementing bullets :309-:310 breaks the transition it promises, and old sessions go blind rather than reconnecting.
findings.text: §13 states "A server started before this lands still compares in its own image, so each session needs one reconnect to pick this up", but the deliverable changes both probe directions: bullet :309 makes the readiness probe report each parameter "with whether each one is required", and bullet :310 makes the parent send its registered parameters (with requiredness) along with the probe. The pre-§13 parent's `_probe_signature_changed` (`reckon/mcp.py:320-325`) requires the probe's per-tool value to be a `list` and returns `False` for anything else, and the pre-§13 probe request carries no registered-parameter payload (`CurrentCodeServer.probe`, `reckon/served_code.py:1569-1571` sends `op=probe` alone). So an already-running session reading a new-shape probe answer decides "unchanged" for every tool and emits no `stale_server_code` at all: no reconnect is ever asked for, the session never picks §13 up, and it silently loses the one refusal §11 left. The plan neither pins the probe answer's wire shape (requiredness added beside the existing name list, or inside it) nor says what the child answers when the probe request carries no registered parameters — the plan's mechanism and its own transition claim are therefore in conflict.

The two "seen by an … session at 05:05Z / 23:47Z" reconnect reports are uncited, the same shape a prior review declined for §11 (cross-session messages have no durable store), so they are not re-raised.
